questions.question: In the period 2, the element having highest Ionisation Potential is Neon because:

options.c: The outermost shell is completely filled

questions.solution: (c) The outermost shell is completely filled. A stable octet makes removal of an electron very difficult.

concepts: dehydration of ethanol by conc. H2SO4
questions.question: The process of conversion of Ethanol to Ethene by the action of concentrated Sulphuric acid involves
questions.solution: (a) Dehydration. Conc. H2SO4 removes a water molecule from ethanol: C2H5OH -> C2H4 + H2O.

concepts: electrolytes conduct due to free ions
questions.question:
Assertion (A): An aqueous solution of Sodium chloride conducts electricity.
Reason (R): Conduction of electric current is due to presence of free ions.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

questions.solution: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. Aqueous NaCl contains free mobile Na+ and Cl- ions which carry the current.

questions.topic: Gram molecular mass from molar volume
questions.question: The mass of 11.2 litres of a certain gas at STP is 32 grams. Find the gram molecular mass of the gas.
questions.solution: (b) 64 g. 22.4 L at STP is 1 mole; 11.2 L = 0.5 mol weighs 32 g, so 1 mol weighs 64 g.

questions.question: The elements are arranged in the increasing order of their metallic character. State which of the arrangements is correct?
questions.solution: (a) Si, Al, Mg, Na. Metallic character decreases across a period from left to right, so in increasing order it is Si < Al < Mg < Na.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common characteristic of a covalent compound?

options.b: They conduct electricity in the molten state
options.c: They are always soluble in water

questions.solution: (d) They consist of molecules. Covalent compounds are made of discrete molecules held by weak intermolecular forces.

questions.question: A metal article is to be plated with Silver and the electrolyte used is Sodium argentocyanide. Choose the correct reaction taking place at the cathode.
questions.solution: (b) Ag+ + 1e -> Ag. At the cathode (the article) Ag+ ions gain electrons and are deposited as silver.

questions.topic: Action of NH4OH on salt solutions
questions.question: A gelatinous white precipitate is formed on addition of small amount of Ammonium hydroxide to this solution and the precipitate dissolves in excess.
questions.solution: (c) ZnSO4. Zn(OH)2 is a gelatinous white precipitate that dissolves in excess NH4OH forming soluble tetraamminezinc(II) sulphate.

questions.question: The ratio between the volume occupied by 32 g of Sulphur dioxide gas and 16 grams of Oxygen gas at STP is: [Atomic weight: S = 32, O = 16]
questions.solution: (d) 1:1. 32 g SO2 = 32/64 = 0.5 mol; 16 g O2 = 16/32 = 0.5 mol. Equal moles occupy equal volumes at STP.

questions.topic: Reactivity of metals down a group
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The tendency to lose electrons increases down a group.
Reason (R): The most reactive metal is placed at the top of Group 1.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

questions.solution: (c) A is true but R is false. Atomic size increases down a group so electrons are lost more easily; hence the most reactive metal is at the bottom of Group 1, not the top.

questions.question: The catalyst used in the manufacturing of Ammonia by Haber's process.
questions.solution: (b) Iron. Finely divided iron (with molybdenum as promoter) is the catalyst in Haber's process.

concepts: lone pairs on oxygen in H2O
questions.question: In the molecule of water, Oxygen atom has
questions.solution: (c) Two lone pair of electrons. Oxygen (2,6) forms two shared pairs with two H atoms and keeps two lone pairs.

questions.question: Ethanol containing about 5% methanol is referred to as ________ alcohol.
questions.solution: (a) Denatured. Ethanol made unfit for drinking by adding about 5% methanol (often sold as methylated spirit) is called denatured alcohol.

questions.question:
The property of Sulphuric acid in the equation given below:
S + 2H2SO4 (conc) -> 3SO2 + 2H2O
questions.solution: (c) Oxidising agent. Conc. H2SO4 oxidises sulphur to SO2 and is itself reduced to SO2.

concepts: anode oxidised by oxygen in Hall-Heroult process
questions.question: During extraction of Aluminium from Bauxite by Hall Heroult's process, the carbon rods are replaced continuously because:

options.b: It minimizes the loss of heat due to radiation
options.d: It enhances the mobility of ions

questions.solution: (c) The carbon anode is consumed. Oxygen liberated at the anode oxidises carbon to CO/CO2, so the anode burns away.

questions.question:
Seema has drawn a diagram representing the preparation of Ammonia in the laboratory. [Diagram: reaction mixture X heated in a round-bottom flask clamped in an inclined position; the gas passes through a drying tower Y and is collected in an inverted gas jar.]
(a) The diagram drawn shows the round bottom flask in an inclined position. Is the diagram drawn by Seema correct? If so, justify.
(b) Given below are two combinations of the reactants. (Ammonium chloride and alkali or Ammonium nitrate and alkali) Select the correct one giving reason why the other combination cannot be used.
(c) Give balanced equation for the laboratory preparation of Ammonia.
(d) Which among the following is used as substance Y. (Conc. H2SO4, P2O5, Fused CaCl2, CaO) State the property of the substance Y.
questions.solution:
(a) Yes, the diagram is correct. The flask is kept inclined so that the water formed during the reaction does not trickle back onto the hot part of the flask and crack it.
(b) Ammonium chloride and alkali (e.g. slaked lime). Ammonium nitrate is not used because it is explosive and decomposes violently on heating (to N2O and water) instead of giving ammonia.
(c) 2NH4Cl + Ca(OH)2 -> CaCl2 + 2H2O + 2NH3
(d) Y is quicklime (CaO). It is a basic drying agent (hygroscopic) that does not react with ammonia, whereas conc. H2SO4 and P2O5 (acidic) react with NH3 and fused CaCl2 forms an addition compound CaCl2.8NH3.

marking_points.point: (a) Correct; inclined so water formed does not run back and crack the hot flask
(b) NH4Cl + alkali chosen; NH4NO3 is explosive on heating
(d) Basic drying agent / does not react with NH3

questions.figure_desc: Laboratory set-up for ammonia: inclined round-bottom flask with mixture X heated, drying tower Y, gas jar collection by downward displacement of air.

questions.question:
State the term for the following:
(a) The process of heating of the ore in limited supply of air.
(b) The tendency of an element to form chains of identical atoms.
(c) The process of separation of ions already in the ionic form.
(d) The formula which represents the simplest ratio between the atoms of elements present in a compound.
(e) The amount of energy required to remove an electron from the outermost shell of an isolated gaseous atom.

answer_items.prompt: Heating of the ore in limited supply of air
Tendency of an element to form chains of identical atoms
Separation of ions already in the ionic form
Formula giving simplest ratio between atoms
Energy required to remove an electron from outermost shell of isolated gaseous atom

questions.solution:
(a) Calcination
(b) Catenation
(c) Dissociation (electrolytic dissociation)
(d) Empirical formula
(e) Ionisation potential (ionisation energy)

Note on (a): heating in a limited supply of air or in the absence of air is calcination; heating in excess air is roasting.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Complete the following by choosing the correct answers from the bracket:
(a) The salt formed by Simple Displacement method is ________. (FeCl2 / FeCl3)
(b) The electron affinity of element X is greater than that of element Y. The reducing power of Y is ______ (more / less) than that of X.
(c) The salt formed when Lead (II) oxide reacts with hot, conc. Sodium hydroxide is ______. (Lead hydroxide / Sodium plumbite)
(d) During the electrolysis of acidulated water, the gas liberated at the anode is ________. (Hydrogen / Oxygen)
(e) Copper and Zinc are alloyed to form ______. (Brass / Bronze)

answer_items.prompt: Salt formed by simple displacement (FeCl2 / FeCl3)
Reducing power of Y compared with X
Salt formed when PbO reacts with hot conc. NaOH
Gas at anode in electrolysis of acidulated water

questions.solution:
(a) FeCl2 (Fe + 2HCl -> FeCl2 + H2)
(b) more (lower electron affinity means greater tendency to lose electrons, so Y is a stronger reducing agent)
(c) Sodium plumbite (PbO + 2NaOH -> Na2PbO2 + H2O)
(d) Oxygen
(e) Brass

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.topic: Types of acids, bases and salts
questions.question:
Match the following Column A with Column B:
Column A: (a) Dibasic acid (b) Acid Salt (c) Mono-acidic base (d) Normal Salt (e) Tri-acidic base
Column B: 1. Sodium chloride 2. Sulphuric acid 3. Aluminium hydroxide 4. Potassium hydroxide 5. Sodium bicarbonate
questions.solution:
(a) Dibasic acid - 2. Sulphuric acid
(b) Acid salt - 5. Sodium bicarbonate
(c) Mono-acidic base - 4. Potassium hydroxide
(d) Normal salt - 1. Sodium chloride
(e) Tri-acidic base - 3. Aluminium hydroxide

questions.question:
Draw the branched structures of the Organic compounds given below:
1. Butanoic acid
2. 2-Pentanol
questions.solution:
1. Butanoic acid: CH3-CH2-CH2-COOH, drawn fully expanded: H3C-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-OH with all C-H bonds shown.
2. 2-Pentanol (pentan-2-ol): CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-CH3, a five-carbon chain with the -OH on carbon 2, all C-H bonds shown.

marking_points.point: Butanoic acid: 4-carbon chain with -COOH, all bonds shown
2-Pentanol: 5-carbon chain with -OH on C-2, all bonds shown

questions.question:
Identify and write the IUPAC names of the Organic compounds shown below:
1. H-C(H)(Br)-C(Br)(H)-H, i.e. BrCH2-CH2Br (each carbon carries one Br and two H)
2. H-C(H)(H)-C(H)(H)-C(=O)H, i.e. CH3-CH2-CHO
3. H3C-C≡C-CH3 (two methyl groups joined by a carbon-carbon triple bond)

1. 1,2-Dibromoethane
2. Propanal
3. But-2-yne (2-butyne)

(b) A white precipitate (underlined) obtained when Lead nitrate is treated with Sodium hydroxide solution.

questions.question: An Organic hydrocarbon referred to as a Green house gas. Name the compound and draw the electron dot diagram for the formation of its molecule.
questions.solution:
Methane (CH4).
Electron dot diagram: carbon (2,4) has 4 valence electrons; each of the four hydrogen atoms shares its one electron with one carbon electron, forming four shared pairs (four single covalent bonds). Carbon attains an octet and each H attains a duplet; no lone pairs on carbon.

marking_points.point: Correct dot diagram: C with four shared pairs with four H atoms

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Give one significant observation when:
(a) Nitric acid is placed in a reagent bottle for a long time.
(b) A solution of Sodium hydroxide is added to Iron (II) sulphate.
(c) Ammonia gas is passed through Copper(II) oxide.
questions.solution:
(a) The colourless acid turns yellow, because it slowly decomposes to give NO2 which dissolves in it: 4HNO3 -> 4NO2 + 2H2O + O2.
(b) A dirty green precipitate of Fe(OH)2 is formed.
(c) Black copper(II) oxide turns reddish brown (copper) and droplets of water form: 3CuO + 2NH3 -> 3Cu + 3H2O + N2.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Define the following terms:
(a) Co-ordinate bond
(b) Isomers
questions.solution:
(a) A co-ordinate bond is a type of covalent bond in which the shared pair of electrons is contributed by only one of the two combining atoms (the donor), e.g. in NH4+ and H3O+.
(b) Isomers are compounds having the same molecular formula but different structural formulae (and hence different properties).

marking_points.point: Coordinate bond: shared pair donated by one atom only
Isomers: same molecular formula, different structural formula

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Arrange the following as per the instructions given in the bracket.
(a) Cl, F, Br, I (in the increasing order of Electron affinity)
(b) NH4OH, H2CO3, H2O, HNO3 (in the increasing order of pH value)

answer_items.prompt: Increasing electron affinity of Cl, F, Br, I
Increasing pH of NH4OH, H2CO3, H2O, HNO3

questions.solution:
(a) I < Br < F < Cl (chlorine has the highest electron affinity; fluorine is lower than chlorine because of its very small size).
(b) HNO3 < H2CO3 < H2O < NH4OH (strong acid < weak acid < neutral < weak base).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
An Organic compound with Vapour density 21. (Atomic weight C = 12, H = 1) Select the molecular formulae from the list of the given below.
(C3H6, C2H4, C2H6, C3H8)
Write the IUPAC name and draw the branched structure of the compound.
questions.solution:
Molecular mass = 2 x VD = 2 x 21 = 42.
C3H6 = 3(12) + 6(1) = 42 (C2H4 = 28, C2H6 = 30, C3H8 = 44). So the compound is C3H6.
IUPAC name: Propene.
Structure: CH2=CH-CH3, drawn with all bonds: H2C=C(H)-C(H)(H)-H.

marking_points.point: Molecular mass = 2 x VD = 42, so C3H6
Structure CH2=CH-CH3 with all bonds shown

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Electron dot structure of calcium oxide
questions.question:
On thermal decomposition of Calcium carbonate, a gas B is liberated with the formation of a compound A. Name the compound A and draw an electron dot diagram to show the formation of the compound.
CaCO3 --(heat)--> A + B
questions.solution:
CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2. A = calcium oxide (CaO), B = carbon dioxide.
Electron dot diagram: Ca (2,8,8,2) transfers its two valence electrons to O (2,6). Ca becomes Ca2+ (2,8,8) and O becomes O2- (2,8) with a complete octet; the ions are held by electrostatic attraction: Ca: + .O. -> [Ca]2+ [:O:]2- (ionic/electrovalent bond).

marking_points.point: Transfer of 2 electrons from Ca to O shown
Ions Ca2+ and O2- with octet shown correctly

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Write balanced chemical equations for the conversions A, B and C.
Fe --(A)--> FeSO4
Fe --(B)--> FeCl3
FeCl3 --(C)--> Fe(OH)3
questions.solution:
(A) Fe + H2SO4 (dil) -> FeSO4 + H2
(B) 2Fe + 3Cl2 --(heat)--> 2FeCl3
(C) FeCl3 + 3NaOH -> Fe(OH)3 (reddish-brown ppt) + 3NaCl (or FeCl3 + 3NH4OH -> Fe(OH)3 + 3NH4Cl)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Moles of product from mass of reactant
questions.question:
Zinc blende is roasted in air. The equation for the same is as given below.
2ZnS + 3O2 --(heat)--> 2ZnO + 2SO2
Calculate the number of moles of Sulphur dioxide liberated by 776 g of ZnS. (S = 32, Zn = 65, O = 16)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of ZnS = 65 + 32 = 97 g/mol.
Moles of ZnS = 776 / 97 = 8 mol.
From the equation, 2 mol ZnS give 2 mol SO2, so 8 mol ZnS give 8 mol SO2.
Answer: 8 moles of SO2.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Correct the statement by adding a word
concepts: ammonia is basic only when moist
questions.question:
Rewrite the statement by adding an appropriate word.
(a) Ammonia changes red litmus to blue.
(b) Magnesium nitride reacts with water to liberate Ammonia.
(c) Conc. Nitric acid is an oxidizing agent.
questions.solution:
(a) Ammonia changes moist red litmus to blue (dry ammonia has no action on dry litmus).
(b) Magnesium nitride reacts with warm water to liberate ammonia. (Mg3N2 + 6H2O -> 3Mg(OH)2 + 2NH3)
(c) Conc. nitric acid is a strong (powerful) oxidizing agent.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Different methods of Preparation of salts are as listed below: (Synthesis, Simple Displacement, Precipitation, Neutralisation)
Choose the most appropriate method used for the preparation of following salts:
(a) CuSO4 (b) CaCO3 (c) AlCl3
questions.solution:
(a) CuSO4 - Neutralisation (CuO + H2SO4 -> CuSO4 + H2O; copper does not displace hydrogen from dilute acids).
(b) CaCO3 - Precipitation (CaCl2 + Na2CO3 -> CaCO3 + 2NaCl; insoluble salt).
(c) AlCl3 - Synthesis / direct combination (2Al + 3Cl2 -> 2AlCl3; anhydrous AlCl3 cannot be obtained from solution as it hydrolyses).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: With reference to Hall Heroult's process of reduction of Aluminium, write the electrolytic reactions at the cathode and anode.
questions.solution:
At cathode: Al3+ + 3e- -> Al (2Al3+ + 6e- -> 2Al)
At anode: O2- - 2e- -> [O]; [O] + [O] -> O2 (the oxygen then oxidises the carbon anode: 2C + O2 -> 2CO, C + O2 -> CO2)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Justify the following statements:
(a) Graphite electrodes are preferred in the electrolysis of fused lead bromide.
(b) Covalent compounds have low melting and boiling point.
questions.solution:
(a) Graphite is inert: it is not attacked by the highly reactive bromine vapour liberated at the anode, whereas an active metal anode would react with bromine. It is also a good conductor and withstands the high temperature.
(b) Covalent compounds consist of molecules held together by weak intermolecular (van der Waals) forces, so little energy is needed to separate them.

marking_points.point: (a) Graphite is inert, not attacked by bromine at the anode

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Reena heated 11.2 g of the element A and 4.8 g of element B to form a compound. Find the Empirical formula of the compound. (Atomic weight: A = 56, B = 16)
questions.solution:
Moles of A = 11.2 / 56 = 0.2
Moles of B = 4.8 / 16 = 0.3
Simplest ratio A : B = 0.2 : 0.3 = 2 : 3
Empirical formula = A2B3 (corresponds to Fe2O3).

Given below is a branched structure of an Organic compound: H-C(H)(H)-C(=O)-OH, i.e. CH3COOH.
(a) Identify and write its IUPAC name of the Organic compound.
(b) In its pure form on cooling, it turns into ice-like crystals. What is it referred to as?

(b) Glacial acetic acid.
(c) Esterification: CH3COOH + C2H5OH --(conc. H2SO4)--> CH3COOC2H5 + H2O (ethyl ethanoate, a sweet-smelling ester).

(a) Give balanced equation for the above reaction.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Electron dot structure of hydronium ion
questions.question: Draw the electron dot diagram for the formation of Hydronium ion.
questions.solution:
H2O + H+ -> H3O+.
Diagram: the oxygen of water (two shared pairs with two H atoms and two lone pairs) donates one of its lone pairs to a hydrogen ion (H+, which has no electrons), forming a coordinate bond. The resulting [H3O]+ shows three shared pairs around O (two covalent, one coordinate) and one lone pair, with an overall +1 charge.

marking_points.point: Water molecule with two lone pairs on O, and H+ shown
Lone pair donated to H+ forming coordinate bond; [H3O]+ with one lone pair and + charge

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Based on the diagram given below, answer the following questions.
[Diagram: an electrolytic cell connected to a battery; the anode (+) is impure copper, the cathode (-) is pure copper, and impurities collect at the bottom below the anode.]
(a) Identify and define the process
(b) Write the reactions at the two electrodes
questions.solution:
(a) Electrorefining (electrolytic refining) of copper. It is the process of purifying an impure metal by electrolysis, in which the impure metal is made the anode, a thin strip of pure metal is the cathode and a solution of a salt of the metal (acidified CuSO4) is the electrolyte; pure metal deposits on the cathode and impurities settle as anode mud.
(b) Cathode: Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu
Anode: Cu - 2e- -> Cu2+

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Write chemical equations for the preparation of the Organic compounds:
(a) Ethane from Sodium propanoate
(b) Ethene from Ethanol
(c) Ethyne from Calcium carbide
questions.solution:
(a) C2H5COONa + NaOH --(CaO, heat)--> C2H6 + Na2CO3 (decarboxylation with soda lime)
(b) C2H5OH --(conc. H2SO4, 170 C)--> C2H4 + H2O
(c) CaC2 + 2H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + C2H2
